text:
michael: perf alert from perf-bot — 99th latency for mixtral-8k up ~2.3x since kernel-selector change at 1719996000
perf-bot: detected increased KV cache miss rate and small tail spikes on tiled-attn path (sampled traces attached)
arya: seeing same on qwen-32k too, but smaller magnitude. root cause looks like prefetch/pipeline misalignment after we enabled dynamic-tiling heuristic
liz: can you paste the pprof flamegraph?
michael: attaching excerpt from a quick profile snapshot:
```
# hot functions
kernel_selector::choose_path  42%
attn_tiler::emit_tiles    18%
kv_cache::evict_check     12%
decoder::dispatch_step     9%
```
sam: hmm kernel_selector now prefers tiled-attn for sequences > 2048 by default; that bumped prefetch distance and changed KV cache access pattern
arya: telemetry shows avg KV cache occupancy down 11% after the change, eviction rate up ~3x. That matches perf-bot
liz: could RoPE scaling interplay be making tiled paths more expensive for certain head dims? we had a special-case for mixtral's 16-head layout in head-align branch
michael: good call. mixtral config uses rope_scale = 1.0 fallback and head_centering enabled. If tiled-attn assumes contiguous KV slices, head-centering might scatter accesses
sam: quick experiment suggestion: revert selector rule for mixtral family only, keep dynamic-tiling for others. low-risk and we can test in canary
arya: i ran a canary on a small shard with selector override: latency back to baseline, KV miss down to previous numbers
perf-bot: sanity-check eval runs: throughput stable, no immediate quality signal changes detected (eval prompts ok)
liz: but watch out — earlier we saw small LM quality diffs when switching kernels on qwen due to fp16 kernel numerics. did you run evals on the failing tests?
michael: yes ran the nightly regression harness against our small prompt set: there are 3 failures — 2 diffs in tokenization boundary cases and 1 hallucination increase on a long-chain QA prompt
sam: that aligns with kernel swap causing slight attention weighting drift; likely due to accumulation order and quantization path differences
arya: proposal: 1) rollback kernel-selector rule for mixtral (canary → prod) 2) add an experiment to test tiled-attn vs fallback for head-centered configs across head dims 3) add KV occupancy metrics to per-model dashboards and alerting
liz: also add a quick unit test in runtime-eval to run a handful of deterministic prompts across both kernels to catch quality regressions automatically
michael: owner = sam for rollback (oncall to schedule); owner = arya for dashboards; owner = liz for eval tests
oncall: starting rollback canary now: `deploy rollback kernel-selector=stable --filter=model:mixtral* --env=canary`
perf-bot: canary started at 1719998902, 120s window
michael: initial canary shows 95p/99p dropping toward baseline in ~30s
arya: KV eviction rate trending down, looks good
liz: running eval suite now against canary outputs — will post results in 5m
perf-bot: eval completed: 3/1200 prompts flagged differences; diffs are small but reproducible on the tiled-attn path
sam: given small but reproducible quality diffs, we should not enable tiled-attn for mixtral until we handle head-centering mismatch in tiled code path. rollback to stable selector for mixtral -> approve? :thumbsup: :thumbsdown:
michael: :thumbsup:
arya: :thumbsup:
liz: :thumbsup: but follow-up ticket required to fix numerics
oncall: rollback to stable selector promoted to prod at 1719998928 for mixtral*
sam: opened GH issue #4521: "tiled-attn head-centering mismatch -> KV scatter -> perf/quality regression" with initial repro and traces
arya: adding perf traces and canary logs to the issue
michael: summary: kernel-selector heuristic caused tiled-attn to win for mixtral, exposing head-centering KV scatter and RoPE/dim mismatch -> increased KV evictions and tail latencies + tiny quality diffs. Rollback done for mixtral, owners assigned for tests, dashboards, and remediation
liz: thanks team. next steps: reproduce locally with a deterministic seed and add the eval gate to CI before we flip selector again
michael: tagging follow-ups in the issue and closing this thread once tickets are linked
